# itsmittalharshit/SAFViT
**Stars**: 0 | **Language**: Jupyter Notebook
**Description**: The SAFViT repository presents a novel Spatial Attention Fusion (SAF) Gating mechanism for Vision Transformer-based nucleus segmentation and classification in histopathology images. This drop-in replacement for conventional skip connections learns a per-pixel 'heatmap of trust' to dynamically balance local encoder details and global decoder context. The architecture, based on CellViT, utilizes a Swin-Tiny encoder and a multi-task decoder with three prediction heads for nuclei presence, instance centroids (HoVer-Net style), and nucleus type classification. SAFViT demonstrates superior performance on the PanNuke dataset, particularly for minority classes, and achieves the highest multi-class panoptic quality compared to various gating strategies.

## README.md
```
# SAFViT: Spatial Attention Fusion Vision Transformer

**Spatial Attention Fusion Gating for Vision Transformer-Based Nucleus Segmentation and Classification**

[Harshit Mittal](mailto:mittalharshit99@gmail.com), Arash Rabbani
School of Computing, University of Leeds

![Graphical Abstract](Images/graphical_Abstract.png)

---

## Overview

SAFViT is a CellViT-based encoder–decoder architecture for **nucleus instance segmentation and classification** in H&E-stained histopathology images. Its core contribution is **Spatial Attention Fusion (SAF) Gating** — a drop-in replacement for conventional skip connections that learns a per-pixel *"heatmap of trust"* deciding, at every spatial location, how much to rely on local encoder detail versus global decoder context.

Unlike standard attention gates that filter only the encoder stream, SAF Gating treats the encoder skip and the upsampled decoder feature as **two equal candidates for fusion**, jointly modulating both with a softmax-normalised, complementary pair of weights. Nothing is discarded — information is only redistributed according to learned spatial reliability.

Evaluated against six alternative gating strategies (no gating / CellViT baseline, Attention Gates, Squeeze-and-Excitation, CBAM, Cross-Attention, and Attentional Feature Fusion) under identical training conditions on **PanNuke**, SAFViT achieves the highest multi-class panoptic quality (**mPQ = 0.471**) and the best F1-score on the difficult, severely underrepresented **Dead** cell class (**F1 = 0.518**), while matching the strongest baselines on Dice, AJI, and bPQ — at effectively zero extra inference cost.

### Highlights

- Proposes Spatial Attention Fusion Gating to build a CellViT-based model, SAFViT.
- Generates a "heatmap of trust" to learn the most trustworthy feature source for each pixel.
- Achieves the highest F1-score for the minority "Dead" class among all gating methods compared.
- Achieves the highest mPQ (0.471) among all compared models, including the ungated baseline.

---

## Architecture

SAFViT retains CellViT's Swin-Tiny encoder / multi-task decoder topology but replaces every skip connection with an SAF Gate.

![SAFViT Architecture](Images/Architecture.png)

- **Encoder:** Swin-Tiny transformer (ImageNet-pretrained), 4 hierarchical stages producing multi-scale features `{E1, E2, E3, E4}` with channel dims `{96, 192, 384, 768}` at resolutions `{56², 28², 14², 7²}` from a `224×224×3` H&E input patch.
- **Decoder:** 3 transposed-convolution upsampling stages, each fusing the decoder stream with the corresponding encoder skip via an **SAF Gate** instead of direct concatenation/addition.
- **Prediction heads** (shared `96×56×56` decoder output feeds all three):
  - **NP head** — binary nuclei-presence mask
  - **HV head** — horizontal/vertical distance maps to instance centroids (HoVer-Net formulation)
  - **NT head** — `(K+1)`-channel nucleus type classification map
- **Post-processing:** HoVer-Net-style watershed instance separation + majority-vote cell typing.

### Spatial Attention Fusion (SAF) Gating

![SAF Gating Module](Images/gating.png)

Given encoder skip features `F_local ∈ R^(C×H×W)` and upsampled decoder features `F_global ∈ R^(C×H×W)`:

1. **Concatenate** the two streams: `F_concat = concat[F_local : F_global] ∈ R^(2C×H×W)`
2. **Bottleneck compression** through two 1×1 convolutions with an intermediate ReLU (`2C → C/2 → 2` channels)
3. **Channel-wise softmax** over the 2-channel output produces complementary trust weights `[w_local ; w_global]`, with `w_local + w_global = 1` at every pixel
4. **Blend:** `F_blend = w_local ⊙ F_local + w_global ⊙ F_global`
5. **Refine** with a `3×3` conv + BatchNorm + ReLU to produce `F_fused`, which replaces the conventional skip output at that decoder level

This guarantees a zero-sum trade-off between local and global reliance — the gate is selective but fully information-preserving, unlike attention gates (encoder-only scalar gating) or SE blocks (channel-only recalibration with no spatial specificity).

**Where the model looks:** at nuclear boundaries — especially the thin, irregular membranes of Dead cells — `w_local` approaches 1.0, showing the gate leans on fine-scale encoder detail exactly where rare-class discrimination is hardest. In homogeneous stromal regions, `w_global` (decoder context) dominates instead.

![Heatmap of Trust](Images/decoder.png)

---

---

## Datasets

| Dataset | Role | Details |
|---|---|---|
| **[PanNuke](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.10778)** | Train / cross-validation | 7,901 pan-cancer H&E patches (256×256, centre-cropped to 224×224) across 19 tissue types; 5 cell classes (Neoplastic, Inflammatory, Connective, Dead, Epithelial); heavy class imbalance |
| **[MoNuSeg](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/8880654)** | Out-of-domain test only (no fine-tuning) | 14 test images (1000×1000) from 7 organs; binary instance masks only, no cell-type labels |

All models are trained under identical conditions — same fold splits, augmentation pipeline (flips, rotation, colour jitter, Gaussian blur, elastic deformation), learning-rate schedule, optimiser, and epoch budget — so that performance differences are attributable solely to the gating mechanism.

---

## Results

### PanNuke (3-fold cross-validation)

| Model | Dice | AJI | bPQ | mPQ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CellViT (baseline) | 0.832 ± .003 | 0.672 ± .004 | 0.625 ± .003 | 0.453 ± .030 |
| **SAFViT (proposed)** | 0.834 ± .003 | 0.674 ± .006 | 0.627 ± .007 | **0.471 ± .032** |
| AG | 0.834 ± .002 | 0.670 ± .005 | 0.620 ± .005 | 0.430 ± .007 |
| SE | 0.833 ± .002 | 0.674 ± .003 | **0.628 ± .001** | 0.457 ± .029 |
| CBAM | 0.834 ± .004 | 0.674 ± .005 | 0.627 ± .003 | 0.453 ± .026 |
| CrossAttn | 0.827 ± .002 | 0.663 ± .005 | 0.608 ± .005 | 0.449 ± .026 |
| AFF | 0.833 ± .003 | 0.670 ± .003 | 0.622 ± .000 | 0.429 ± .001 |

### Per-class F1 (out-of-fold, PanNuke)

| Model | Neoplastic | Inflammatory | Connective | **Dead** | Epithelial |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CellViT | 0.902 | 0.801 | 0.781 | 0.373 | 0.898 |
| **SAFViT** | 0.903 | 0.790 | **0.782** | **0.518** | 0.898 |
| AG | 0.898 | 0.790 | 0.778 | 0.000 | 0.895 |
| SE | 0.903 | 0.800 | 0.781 | 0.295 | 0.903 |
| CBAM | 0.898 | 0.792 | 0.777 | 0.364 | 0.900 |
| CrossAttn | 0.892 | 0.773 | 0.756 | 0.462 | 0.885 |
| AFF | 0.893 | 0.785 | 0.778 | 0.000 | 0.881 |

Two encoder-only gating variants (AG, AFF) **completely fail** on the Dead class (F1 = 0.000); SAFViT's dual-stream gating gives it the largest margin over the ungated baseline on this rare category (+14.5 points), which drives its mPQ lead.

### MoNuSeg (out-of-domain, zero fine-tuning)

| Model | Dice | AJI | Inference (ms/img) |
|---|---|---|---|
| CellViT | 0.738 ± .033 | 0.539 ± .035 | 5.8 |
| SAFViT | 0.737 ± .033 | 0.540 ± .035 | 5.7 |
| AG | **0.745 ± .028** | **0.544 ± .031** | 5.6 |
| SE | 0.740 ± .033 | 0.542 ± .035 | 5.6 |
| CBAM | 0.739 ± .032 | 0.542 ± .034 | 5.6 |
| CrossAttn | 0.741 ± .030 | 0.541 ± .034 | 5.6 |
| AFF | 0.740 ± .031 | 0.542 ± .034 | 5.7 |

MoNuSeg's binary-only annotations can't capture multi-class discrimination — precisely where SAFViT's advantage lies — so all models cluster closely here. All seven variants run in **5.6–5.8 ms/image**, confirming SAF Gating's two pointwise convolutions add negligible parameters and no measurable latency versus the ungated baseline.

### Statistical significance (Wilcoxon signed-rank, per-image, N = 7,901)

SAFViT significantly outperforms **AG, AFF, and CrossAttn** on AJI (p < 0.05, and p ≪ 0.001 for AG/CrossAttn), and shows a significant but modest AJI/Dice advantage over the ungated **CellViT** baseline. SAFViT is statistically indistinguishable from **SE** and **CBAM** on both Dice and AJI, consistent with the narrow numeric gaps above — the meaningful separation between methods shows up in mPQ / Dead-class F1, not in class-agnostic overlap metrics.

## Evaluation Metrics

- **Dice** — pixel-level overlap between predicted and ground-truth binary nuclear masks
- **AJI** (Aggregated Jaccard Index) — instance-level one-to-one matching aggregated IoU, penalising missed/spurious detections
- **bPQ** (Binary Panoptic Quality) — class-agnostic detection (F1 @ IoU ≥ 0.5) × segmentation quality (mean matched IoU)
- **mPQ** (Multi-class Panoptic Quality) — bPQ computed per class and averaged; equal class weighting makes it the metric most sensitive to rare-class performance (e.g. Dead)
- **Inference time** — ms/image, confirming SAF Gating's negligible computational overhead

---

## Compared Gating Mechanisms

All seven models share the same Swin-Tiny encoder, decoder topology, three prediction heads, composite loss, and training protocol — the **only** difference is the skip-connection fusion strategy:

| Name | Mechanism |
|---|---|
| **CellViT** | Ungated baseline (direct skip connection) |
| **SAFViT (proposed)** | Spatial Attention Fusion (SAF) Gating — dual-stream, per-pixel softmax heatmap of trust |
| **AG** | Attention Gate (Oktay et al., 2018) — encoder-only scalar attention |
| **SE** | Squeeze-and-Excitation (Hu et al., 2018) — global channel recalibration |
| **CBAM** | Convolutional Block Attention Module (Woo et al., 2018) — channel + spatial attention |
| **CrossAttn** | Gated cross-attention (Jia et al., 2024) |
| **AFF** | Attentional Feature Fusion (Dai et al., 2020) |

---

## Limitations & Future Work

- The Dead class comprises fewer than 2% of annotated PanNuke instances, so small absolute gains translate into large relative F1 changes; the 14.5-point improvement is consistent across all three CV folds, but validation on a dataset with higher Dead-class prevalence would strengthen the finding further.
- The current SAF Gating bottleneck ratio (`2C → C/2 → 2`) is fixed across all decoder levels; an adaptive or level-specific compression strategy could allocate more capacity where the encoder–decoder feature gap is largest.
- SAF Gating is architecture-agnostic and could be integrated into larger pretrained encoders beyond Swin-Tiny.
